name: DYT1 Generalized Dystonia

criteria.description: Presence of pathogenic TOR1A gene mutation (ΔGAG deletion)
Early-onset dystonia with initial limb involvement progressing to generalized dystonia
Positive family history of dystonia or related movement disorders
Exclusion of secondary causes of dystonia such as drug-induced or structural lesions

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Pathogenic TOR1A mutation plus characteristic clinical presentation with exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis; clinical variability exists even within families.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically begins in a limb and spreads to involve multiple body regions

pathognomonic.symptomName: Sustained muscle contractions causing twisting and repetitive movements
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic of dystonia affecting posture and movement

common.symptomName: Limb dystonia with foot or hand involvement
common.notes: Usually the initial site of symptom onset

common.symptomName: Impaired gait due to dystonic posturing

common.notes: Involuntary neck muscle contractions causing abnormal head postures
Due to involvement of oromandibular muscles

occasional.notes: Involuntary movements affecting jaw and tongue

occasional.symptomName: Psychiatric symptoms including anxiety and depression
occasional.notes: May be secondary to chronic disability
Occasionally reported but not a primary feature

rare.notes: Patient-specific maneuvers that transiently reduce symptoms

imaging: Brain MRI typically normal or may show subtle basal ganglia abnormalities
Functional imaging (PET/SPECT) may show altered basal ganglia activity
genetic: Pathogenic ΔGAG deletion mutation in the TOR1A gene on chromosome 9q34
other: Electromyography (EMG) may show co-contraction of antagonist muscles during dystonic movements

distinguishingFeatures: More frequent cranial involvement early in disease
History of drug exposure or brain injury

redFlags: Rapid progression of dystonia with systemic symptoms
Onset after age 30 with atypical features
Poor or no response to standard dystonia treatments
references: Ozelius LJ, et al. The early-onset torsion dystonia gene (DYT1) encodes an ATP-binding protein. Nat Genet. 1997.
Fahn S. Concept and classification of dystonia. Adv Neurol. 1988.
Bressman SB. Dystonia genotypes, phenotypes, and classification. Adv Neurol. 2004.
